title: Resum outside faults before bounding a minimum-weight decoder
statement: For a single consistent family,H(T,Z)=sum_(UsubsetZ)(-1)^|U|Bad(TunionU). Inclusive norms bound this forced/forbidden sum without positivity, independence or commutation. A summed syndrome-selector decoder is CP/TNI with complete norm<=1, avoiding one norm cost per syndrome. Encoded support plus minimum weight forces at least half of each nonzero component into declared fault support; only then does the connected-component bound control identity error.

requires: Actual CPTP total channel and one consistent signed fault family with inclusive complete-norm control
Encoded-support Pauli-pair representation on actual encoded input, check graph, code distance and total support incidence
Perfect final full-syndrome extraction, minimum-weight correction and decoder; exact physical tensor-factor qualification for the Gaussian specialization

assumptions: Acceptance has disclosed author/reviewer overlap in the hereditary-hybrid contribution; it is a completed internal review at this conditional model/receiver scope. Encoded support does not follow from inclusive norm alone. D counts TOTAL experiment incidence, not instantaneous degree. Perfect global final decoder/extraction costs and faults are excluded. DATA baths start factorized and nominal Hamiltonian acts trivially on them, separately from the strong clock environment. Finite-window/static correctness is not indefinitely repeated reused-bath lifetime or a calibrated physical threshold. Ordinary Han/AGP receivers and bounded-Hamiltonian hereditary Duhamel comparisons remain granted.

Coupling/window/correlation parameters, well-defined Wick dynamics, fixed source supports, apparatus/calibration costs
Physical epsilon depends on the whole finite window; no repeated-window bath reset is granted
